page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head centred at the top, page number at the top right. No marginal notes. Gathering signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: feptem? dicent, quoniam semper poteft voluntas nolle, etiam posita gratia sufficientissi-mâ. Resp. 1. Tum etiam in remorione[?] trium graduum duritei[?], poteft voluntas nolle. Ergo gratia nullos omnino gradus removebit, contra scripturas adhuc. 2. Esto, remaneat potentia purae naturae, gratia potentiae adhaerentem contumaciam & duritiem removeat oportet: ea enim est cordis (ut sic loquar) lapidofitas. Quo casu si illa potentia purae naturae exercebit actum purum naturalem nolendi, tum fieri poteft, ut homo resistat Deo vocanti, & non peccet, quod absurdum est. 3. Posse ponere obicem Deo vocanti, vel est corruptio: & sic actus ponendi obicem, per eandem rationem erit peccatum, vel non est corruptio posse Deo reluctari vocanti: sed tum quaero an lapideum cor nihil sit nisi actualis resistentia, & non curvitas potentiae. Si sit tantum actualis resistentia, tum Deus auferendo cor lapideum aufert τὸ actu resistere, quod Arminiani negabunt. Si dixerint Deum auferre τὸ actu resistere ex hypothesi, cedo hypothesin, nempe quod actu non restiterint: si vel malleo cerebra contuderint, hypothesin non dabunt. 4. Nihil vitiositatis inesse potentiae voluntatis, aut nihil vitiositatis habitualis nobis post lapsum inesse, nemo nisi Pelagius diceret. At si aliquid infit, an non removetur, quando removetur cor lapideum? 5. Si natura libertatis talis sit

page.notes: The left margin shows a small printed mark ("P") at the foot, left of the signature; it is not part of the text and is not transcribed. Greek τὸ is copied as printed; its accent and breathing are uncertain. Lines 3 and 5 contain a long-s-like form that is transcribed as a plain s. Three words are marked [?]: "remorione" (possibly "remotione"), "duritei" (possibly "duritiei"), and the first Greek τὸ in line 11 is uncertain. The text is cut off at the foot by the catchword "ut", which begins the next page.
